## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vandanavimānavatthu* (Vv 49) is a short verse narrative included in the *Vimānavatthu* section of the Pali Canon. In this discourse, a celestial being (*deva*) describes the past actions that led to rebirth in a heavenly mansion, explaining how paying homage, worshipping, and honoring Buddhist monastics produces vast merit.

 According to automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus, the text shares extensive formulaic verse segments with other narratives in the collection, most notably the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), as well as the *Dutiyasuṇisāvimānavatthu* (Vv 14), *Caturitthivimānavatthu* (Vv 45), *Bhikkhādāyakavimānavatthu* (Vv 70), and *Alomavimānavatthu* (Vv 42) [DharmaNexus]. Its verses are also incorporated and explained in the commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, with additional reuse found in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records a low-confidence cross-language alignment with a segment of the Tibetan translation of the *Upāyakauśalya-sūtra* (D 261) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
